en: Sappaṭighaduka (The Pair on the Possessing Resistance)
Dependent on a state that is not impinging, a state that is not impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not impinging, a state that is non-impinging arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not impinging, states that are both not impinging and non-impinging arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-reactive state, a non-reactive state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on both a non-obstructive and a non-reactive state, a non-obstructive state arises by way of root condition … three. (Abbreviated.
Nine under root; one under object … pe … nine under non-disappearance.
(The Chapter on Co-nascence ... [and] the Chapter on Association are the same as the Chapter on Dependence.
A non-reactive state is a condition for a non-reactive state by way of root-condition.
A non-reactive state is a condition for a non-obstructive state by way of root-condition. A non-reactive state is a condition for a non-reactive state...
And [it is] a condition for a non-reactive state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

A non-reactive state is a condition for a non-reactive state by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). A non-reactive state is a condition for a non-reactive state by way of the object-condition. (Abbreviated.

There are three [conditions] in the case of the root, two in the case of the object, four in the case of the predominance, one in the case of the immediate, ... [and so on] ... nine in the case of the conascent (*sahajāta*).
Six by mutuality; nine by dependence; two by strong-dependence; three by prenascence and postnascence;
one by repetition; [one] by kamma ... [etc. ... three by nutriment; five by faculty; three by jhāna and path; one by association;
four by dissociation ... [etc. ... nine by non-disappearance.
